title: Observation or Measurement Sorter
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Judge twelve statements about the environment as qualitative observation or quantitative data, with two deliberately tricky cards that break the belief that "has a number" is enough.

learningObjectives: Judge whether a statement about the environment is a qualitative observation or quantitative data.
Justify the judgement by identifying whether both a number and a unit are present.
prerequisites: No prior knowledge required - this is the first MicroSim in the book

keyQuestions: What is missing from "The temperature is 25."?
Can an observation be expert and still not be data?
Why does a unit matter as much as a number?
commonMisconceptions: Believing any sentence containing a digit is quantitative.
Treating "qualitative" as a polite word for "worthless".
Assuming a technical-sounding sentence must be a measurement.
assessmentOpportunities: Applies the number-and-unit rule rather than guessing from how technical the sentence sounds.
Correctly classifies "The temperature is 25." as an observation and explains why.
Accepts that a qualitative observation can be skilled and useful and still not be data.
